name: SH1106 1.3" 128×64 OLED display (I2C)
description: 1.3 inch monochrome 128×64 OLED driven by a Sino Wealth SH1106 controller (132×64 RAM, the panel shows columns 2–129) over I2C at address 0x3C. The module has its own 3.3 V regulator and runs on 3.0–5.0 V. Sold as: AZ-Delivery 1.3 inch OLED I2C Display 128×64 (SH1106, 4-pin header in this order: VDD, GND, SCK (= I2C SCL), SDA), and the many identical 4-pin 1.3" I2C clones.
eli5: A small, sharp black-and-white screen that your board can draw text and pictures on using just two wires.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 3.0–5.0 V (on-board 3.3 V regulator; use 3.3 V on a Raspberry Pi)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (printed "SCK" on the AZ-Delivery board, "SCL" on most clones); pull-up fitted on the module

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data; pull-up fitted on the module

supplierQuery: 1.3 inch OLED SH1106 128x64 I2C 4 pin module
buildNotes: Check the pin order printed on your board: the AZ-Delivery module is VDD, GND, SCK(SCL), SDA, but many other 1.3" I2C modules (e.g. The Pi Hut's) are GND, VCC, SCL, SDA. Swapping VCC and GND destroys the module.

The SH1106 is not an SSD1306: it has 132 RAM columns and no horizontal addressing mode. A SSD1306 driver shows a shifted picture with a garbage stripe; use the sh1106.py driver, which writes each page from column 2.
I2C address 0x3C (7-bit). Some boards have a solder jumper for 0x3D.
Fully lit the panel draws about 40 mA at 3.3 V; power it from the 3V3 or 5V pin, not a GPIO.
OLEDs burn in: blank the screen or call poweroff() when nothing needs to be shown for a long time.

driver.code:
# SH1106 132x64 OLED controller (Sino Wealth), MicroPython I2C driver for 1.3" 128x64 modules.
# Command set and power-on sequence from the SH1106 datasheet V2.3:
#   I2C control byte: Co (bit 7) and D/C (bit 6); 0x80 = one command byte follows, 0x40 = display data follows.
#   The SH1106 has 132 RAM columns; 1.3" 128-pixel panels show columns 2..129, so each page is written from column 2.
#   Page addressing only (B0h-B7h page, 00h-0Fh / 10h-1Fh column): the SH1106 has no 20h/21h/22h address-window commands.
import time
import framebuf


class SH1106_I2C(framebuf.FrameBuffer):
    def __init__(self, width, height, i2c, addr=0x3C, col_offset=2):
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.col_offset = col_offset
        self.pages = height // 8
        self.buffer = bytearray(self.pages * width)
        super().__init__(self.buffer, width, height, framebuf.MONO_VLSB)
        self.init_display()

    def cmd(self, c):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes((0x80, c)))

    def init_display(self):
        for c in (
            0xAE,              # display off (sleep)
            0xD5, 0x80,        # clock divide ratio 1, oscillator +15 %
            0xA8, self.height - 1,  # multiplex ratio
            0xD3, 0x00,        # display offset 0
            0x40,              # display start line 0
            0xAD, 0x8B,        # DC-DC control: built-in DC-DC on (needed by these modules)
            0x32,              # charge pump output 8.0 V (POR)
            0xA1,              # segment re-map: column 131 -> SEG0 (module orientation)
            0xC8,              # COM scan COM[N-1] -> COM0
            0xDA, 0x12,        # common pads: alternative (POR)
            0x81, 0x80,        # contrast 128 (POR)
            0xD9, 0x22,        # discharge/precharge 2/2 DCLKs (POR)
            0xDB, 0x35,        # VCOM deselect level (POR)
            0xA4,              # display follows RAM
            0xA6,              # normal (not inverted)
        ):
            self.cmd(c)
        # Clear all 132 RAM columns of every page (datasheet: clear RAM before display on)
        blank = b'\x40' + bytes(132)
        for page in range(8):
            self.cmd(0xB0 | page)
            self.cmd(0x00)
            self.cmd(0x10)
            self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, blank)
        self.cmd(0xAF)         # display on
        time.sleep_ms(100)     # datasheet: wait 100 ms after display on before sending data
        self.fill(0)
        self.show()

    def poweroff(self):
        self.cmd(0xAE)

    def poweron(self):
        self.cmd(0xAF)

    def contrast(self, value):
        self.cmd(0x81)
        self.cmd(value & 0xFF)

    def invert(self, on):
        self.cmd(0xA7 if on else 0xA6)

    def show(self):
        col = self.col_offset
        for page in range(self.pages):
            self.cmd(0xB0 | page)
            self.cmd(col & 0x0F)
            self.cmd(0x10 | (col >> 4))
            start = page * self.width
            self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, b'\x40' + self.buffer[start:start + self.width])

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sh1106 import SH1106_I2C

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=400000)
oled = SH1106_I2C(128, 64, i2c)
oled.fill(0)
oled.text('Hello 1.3in', 0, 0)
oled.text('SH1106 OLED', 0, 16)
oled.text('128x64 I2C', 0, 32)
oled.show()
print('drawn')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
